plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers. The blooms hum with bees and perfume the warm summer air. In the fields of Provence they form rippling purple rows that stretch to the horizon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August in the Northern Hemisphere, usually peaking in July
plants.location: Provence, southern France, and Mediterranean-climate gardens across Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its name likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, elegant blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, waxy leaves that float on still ponds and lakes. Each flower opens at dawn in soft layers of pink petals around a golden seed pod.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, typically June through August in temperate East Asia
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across Japan, China and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves are covered in microscopic bumps that make water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt with it. Scientists call this the 'lotus effect' and have copied it in self-cleaning coatings.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. Butterflies and goldfinches flock to them in prairies and cottage gardens at the height of summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to September, usually at its best in July
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from prairies to home gardens
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog, a nod to the prickly central cone. Many Native American peoples used the plant medicinally.
